summary: VFDP-15 is a governance/funding proposal from the VITA-FAST decentralized science project seeking approval to modify their 2025 experiment plan. Following H1 2025 NCE testing results at Newcastle University, the team identified two autophagy-inducing protein targets and proposes to pivot toward computational optimization of their VF-series compounds against Autophagy1 and Autophagy2 targets. The budget request covers $11K in additional reagents and MedChem subcontract extension, drawing from an existing $147,500K project wallet.

content_blocks.title: VFDP-15 Proposal Header & TLDR
content_blocks.content: Title: VFDP-15 - Approval for modified VITA-FAST experiment plan 2025. Edited 10/09/2025. TLDR: Following results in H1, the team wants to modify the plan and budget of the upcoming series of experiments to focus on computational optimisation with the now known targets.

content_blocks.title: Background: VITA-FAST Project Overview
content_blocks.content: VITA-FAST is developing new autophagy-inducing compounds for potential therapeutic applications and systemic cellular longevity. In March 2025 (VFDP-13), experiments and budget totalling $135K were scoped for development of new chemical entities (NCEs). The plan covered ordering and testing of two rounds of NCEs (round 2 and round 3) as well as ancillary and confirmatory experiments in worms and human aging cell lines.

content_blocks.title: Key Experimental Results from H1 2025 (Newcastle NCE Testing)
content_blocks.content: Following the 2nd round of NCE testing and target discovery experiments at Newcastle University, the team found: (1) A strong hypothesis of two targets (Autophagy1 and Autophagy2 protein families) that are causing increased autophagy. (2) The structural modifications tested in round 2 of NCEs were not binding these targets any more potently than those in the first round. This provides two critical pieces of information: (a) The 1st target is now known, and a strong hypothesis exists on the 2nd target — these are targets of molecules that fulfil VITA-FAST's mission to induce 10x more autophagy than rapamycin. (b) The chemical moieties tested in round 2 do not contribute to target binding. Footnote clarifies: Autophagy1 is a confirmed target; Autophagy2 is a second family of proteins whose binding activates autophagy, but the specific member is not yet known.

content_blocks.title: Objective
content_blocks.content: To use the target information to develop VITA-FAST compounds to a lead candidate, with a target identified and understanding of mechanistic basis of the compounds' healthspan and longevity effects on human cells. These experiments should allow definition of lead molecule(s) for subsequent IND-enabling activities such as murine safety experiments. IP will also be filed for these compounds. Project milestones targeted: (1) Lead compound, (2) Target ID, (3) Intellectual property — to raise further financing and move compounds into mammals and towards humans.

content_blocks.title: Plan: Cancellation of Previously Approved Experiments
content_blocks.content: Proposal to cancel experiments approved in VFDP-13 that have not yet been performed: (1) Worm longevity at Ora Biomedical, (2) Aging cell lines at Newcastle, (3) Worm healthspan at Magnitude Biosciences, (4) 3rd round SAR NCE Synthesis. Note: these are not bad experiments, just not appropriate given current information. To date, $56,620 of the $135K budgeted in VFDP-13 has been spent. The remaining budget is being replanned.

content_blocks.title: New Experiments Plan
content_blocks.content: The new plan consists of two components: (1) Conduct confirmatory experiments to confirm which of the Autophagy2 protein family is most important — to be done through siRNA knockouts and computational modelling at Newcastle University. (2) Computationally optimise the VF series novel compounds against the Autophagy1 and Autophagy2 targets to generate a highly potent compound now that drug <> target binding can be modelled. After completion, the team will most likely order the computationally optimised compound as an NCE for lab testing, with a plan update at that time.

content_blocks.title: Cost Implications & Budget
content_blocks.content: Original VFDP-13 budget: $135K. Spent to date: $56,620. Next steps can be conducted within existing resources at the University of Newcastle and with medicinal chemist subcontractor Dr Johannes Reynisson, Lecturer in Drug Discovery at the University of Keele (originally added in VFDP-4). Project wallet value: $147,500K as of 2nd Sep 2025 (accounting for allocated but unrealised costs), sufficient to fund this plan and follow-on experiments.

content_blocks.title: Budget Request Table
content_blocks.content:
Two line items requested:
1. Additional siRNA reagents ordered @Newcastle — Cost: $3K — Months: Aug–Dec
2. Extension of MedChem subcontract — Cost: $8K — Months: Jul–Dec
Total new budget requested: $11K

content_blocks.title: Recommendation
content_blocks.content: VITA-FAST has developed potent and novel compounds. This proposal seeks to leverage computational development of those molecules at a highly efficient price point utilising suppliers already in place with quotes from each. Recommended as a highly efficient way of improving the VF series compounds to generate value in the VITA-FAST project and raise further funding.

content_blocks.content: A project data update to describe the results that led to this conclusion will be given in September. A project update on the [document appears cut off].

content_blocks.title: Governance / Voting
content_blocks.content: Community vote on the proposal: 1 vote cast, 100% Yes, 0% No. No end date specified for the vote.

key_findings: VITA-FAST compounds have been confirmed to induce autophagy at 10x the level of rapamycin, with two protein targets (Autophagy1 confirmed, Autophagy2 hypothesised) identified as the mechanism of action.
Round 2 NCE structural modifications did not improve target binding potency vs. Round 1, informing a pivot away from SAR-based NCE synthesis toward computational optimisation.
Target discovery experiments conducted at Newcastle University in H1 2025 provided strong mechanistic hypotheses for both Autophagy1 and Autophagy2 protein families.
The project is at an early lead optimisation stage (pre-IND), with IND-enabling murine safety studies identified as the next major downstream milestone after lead compound identification.
IP filing is planned for the lead compounds once identified through computational optimisation.
MedChem subcontractor Dr Johannes Reynisson (Lecturer in Drug Discovery, University of Keele) is engaged for computational drug-target binding modelling.
siRNA knockouts and computational modelling at Newcastle University will be used to confirm which Autophagy2 protein family member is most relevant.
Project wallet stands at $147,500K as of 2 Sep 2025; $56,620 of $135K previously approved budget has been spent.
Previously approved experiments (worm longevity at Ora Biomedical, aging cell lines at Newcastle, worm healthspan at Magnitude Biosciences, 3rd round SAR NCE synthesis) are proposed for cancellation.
The project is governed via a decentralised voting mechanism (VFDP proposals); this proposal received 100% Yes with 1 vote.
